newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends slightly weaker in late trading.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends slightly weaker in late trading.

text.p: LME copper prices closed a touch lower on Monday in an effort to consolidate losses after losing momentum from an earlier stab at $2,379 a tonne.
At 1910 GMT three months copper was indicated at $2,336/40 after a kerb close of $2,345, $11 weaker.
The market shrugged off news from Chile's Minera Escondida that February copper production reached 63,795 tonnes, lower than the 65,881 tonnes reported for February 1996.
In its evening report, brokerage Brandeis said the small expected decline in LME copper stocks of between 2,000 and 3,000 tonnes might not be enough to counter chart-based selling.
This would see prices returning to examine support at $2,330 and more crucially at $2,313, it said.
Aluminium also ended slightly weaker on the day and was last indicated at $1,661/64 after its unchanged kerb close of $1,668.
